checks: Halfspace-depth superlevels are convex for the whole measure. Exchange of coordinates preserves both components, so taking the midpoint of a mark and its swap cannot reduce depth. Outside the compact support T a separating halfspace has zero mass.
For t≤δ the lower sum-cap costs at most 1/5+(16/5)δ². For t≥δ that cap contains all of δT, while the cap x₁≥t has zero inner-component mass, including its vertex-only trace at t=δ.
On [δ,1/2] the lower sum-cap cost is increasing and the coordinate cap cost is decreasing. Their intersection solves 12t²+8t−3=0, giving t*=(√13−2)/6 in the interval.

Independent exact arithmetic in Q(√13) gave the common value (77−16√13)/45. The small-t bound is below 13/45 and 57²=3249<3328=16²·13 gives the strict comparison to 4/9. The certificate is an upper bound; the proof never identifies an exact optimizer for depth.
